paper.title_en: Decomposing neural decoders: an exactly-anchored benchmark for quantum error correction
paper.abstract_en: Minimum-weight perfect matching (MWPM) is the dominant surface-code decoder but is suboptimal under depolarizing noise, because it discards the $X$-$Z$ correlation that $Y$ errors induce and is not degeneracy-aware. We present an exactly anchored diagnostic benchmark for the code-capacity depolarizing channel, not a case for neural decoding. Five decoders (MWPM, correlated matching, belief-matching, belief propagation with ordered-statistics decoding (BP+OSD) and a lightweight multilayer perceptron (MLP)) are compared with an exact analytic maximum-likelihood (ML) reference at distance $d = 3$, with exact per-syndrome ML decisions on sampled syndromes at $d = 5$, and with a matched-marginal independent-noise control. Measuring MWPM's suboptimality by the relative logical-error-rate (LER) reduction that ML achieves over it, the difference between the depolarizing and control channels is 19-32 percentage points (pp) above an 11%-14% floor at $d = 3$, and 33-60 pp above an 8%-10% floor at $d = 5$. At $d = 3$ the MLP recovers 90%-95% of the MWPM-to-ML gap, more than belief-matching (82%-89%), BP+OSD (74%-80%) or correlated matching (46%-58%). At $d = 5$ belief-matching and BP+OSD agree closely yet stay measurably above ML, recovering 79%-91% of the gap, while the MLP's advantage over MWPM depends on the training budget (crossover near $3.5\times10^{5}$ samples at $p = 0.08$) and, when adequately trained, recovers at most 17%. In simulated circuit-level memory experiments at $d = 3$ and 5, the classical decoders keep their advantage over MWPM, the matched-marginal split becomes decomposition-dependent, and the MLP recovers 25% of the gap at $d = 3$, $T = 2$ and, over five training seeds and budgets up to $9\times10^{5}$ samples, stays an order of magnitude worse than MWPM at $d = 5$, $T = 5$, with or without validation-based early stopping. Per-shot cost grows 33-97-fold for the BP-based decoders but less than twofold for matching, and batched throughput does not bound latency.
